outline.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash
outline.content: Introduce the difference between average speed and instantaneous speed using a high-energy visual. Establish the core question: How do we measure speed at a single, frozen moment in time?
outline.example: A cheetah (named 'Swift') chases a gazelle. We see a stopwatch. Swift covers 100 meters in 4 seconds (Average Speed = 25m/s). But at exactly 2.5 seconds, Swift hits a patch of sand and slows down slightly. How do we find his speed at that exact millisecond?

outline.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
outline.content: Briefly review the 'Rise over Run' concept. Explain that for a straight line, the rate of change (slope) is constant. Use a Position-Time graph to show a linear relationship.
outline.example: A robot moving at a constant pace. The graph is a straight diagonal line. Slope = (Change in Position) / (Change in Time). This is the 'Average Rate of Change' which is easy to calculate because the line never bends.

outline.title: The Paradox of the Single Point
outline.content: Transition to a curved graph (parabola) representing acceleration. Show that calculating speed at one point (t) using the slope formula leads to 0/0 (undefined), creating a mathematical 'roadblock'.
outline.example: Zoom into Swift the Cheetah's curved position graph. If we try to find the slope at point A by using only point A, our formula becomes (Position A - Position A) / (Time A - Time A) = 0/0. The screen flashes a warning sign.

outline.title: The Visual Solution: The Shrinking Secant
outline.content: Introduce the 'Limit' concept through animation. Place a second point (B) near point (A) and draw a secant line. Slowly slide point B toward point A, showing the secant line turning into a tangent line.
outline.example: Imagine a camera lens zooming into the curve. As point B moves closer to A, the gap 'h' shrinks. The line connecting them tilts until it perfectly grazes the curve at just one point. This 'Tangent Line' represents the Instantaneous Rate of Change.

outline.title: Formalizing the Derivative
outline.content: Define the derivative formula. Explain that the derivative is simply the function that gives us the slope of the tangent line at any point x. Emphasize the notation f'(x).
outline.example: Show the formula: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Use a color-coded overlay on the graph: Green for the change in height, Blue for the shrinking distance 'h'. As h disappears, the 'Derivative' is born.

outline.title: Real-World Application: The Speedometer
outline.content: Connect the abstract math back to reality. Explain that every time we look at a car's speedometer, we are looking at a live calculation of a derivative.
outline.example: A dashboard of a sports car. As the car accelerates, the needle moves. The needle isn't showing average speed over the whole trip; it's showing the derivative of the car's position with respect to time at that exact heartbeat.

outline.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
outline.content: Briefly review the 'Rise over Run' concept. Explain that for a straight line, the rate of change (slope) is constant. Use a Position-Time graph to show a linear relationship.
outline.example: A robot moving at a constant pace. The graph is a straight diagonal line. Slope = (Change in Position) / (Change in Time). This is the 'Average Rate of Change' which is easy to calculate because the line never bends.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
lecture_lines: For a straight line, the slope is always constant.
We calculate it using the simple rise over run.
This value represents the constant average rate of change.
animations: A straight diagonal line appears on a Position-Time graph.
Vertical 'Rise' in green (#00FF00) and horizontal 'Run' in blue (#0000FF) appear.
The formula 'Slope = Rise / Run' appears in yellow (#FFFF00).

outline.title: The Paradox of the Single Point
outline.content: Transition to a curved graph (parabola) representing acceleration. Show that calculating speed at one point (t) using the slope formula leads to 0/0 (undefined), creating a mathematical 'roadblock'.
outline.example: Zoom into Swift the Cheetah's curved position graph. If we try to find the slope at point A by using only point A, our formula becomes (Position A - Position A) / (Time A - Time A) = 0/0. The screen flashes a warning sign.

storyboard.title: The Paradox of the Single Point
lecture_lines: Acceleration creates a curved path on our position graph.
Calculating slope at one point leads to zero over zero.
This undefined result creates a challenging mathematical roadblock.
animations: A curved parabola represents increasing speed over time.

The formula '0 / 0' flashes in red (#FF0000) near the point.

Show 'Average Speed = 25m/s' in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Speedometer", [
            "A car's speedometer shows your speed at every heartbeat.",
            "It continuously calculates the derivative of your position.",
            "Calculus connects abstract math to our everyday movement."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Build the Speedometer
        # Outer Arc
        speedo_arc = Arc(
            radius=1.5, 
            start_angle=225 * DEGREES, 
            angle=-270 * DEGREES, 
            color=GRAY_A
        )
        
        # Ticks
        ticks = VGroup()
        for i in range(11):
            angle = (225 - i * 27) * DEGREES
            start = [np.cos(angle) * 1.35, np.sin(angle) * 1.35, 0]
            end = [np.cos(angle) * 1.5, np.sin(angle) * 1.5, 0]
            ticks.add(Line(start, end, color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2))
        
        speedometer = VGroup(speedo_arc, ticks)
        # Use B3-E6 to keep gap (B021)
        self.place_in_area(speedometer, "B3", "E6")
        center_point = speedometer.get_center()

        # Needle
        needle = Line(ORIGIN, [1.2, 0, 0], color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        needle.move_to(center_point, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        needle.rotate(225 * DEGREES, about_point=center_point)
        
        self.play(Create(speedometer), Create(needle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(CYAN)
        )
        
        # Needle sweeps upward
        # Use a ValueTracker for the angle to simulate "continuous calculation"
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(225)
        needle.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value() * DEGREES).move_to(center_point, aligned_edge=LEFT))
        
        # Labels
        speedo_label = Text("Instantaneous Speed = Derivative", font_size=20, color=CYAN)
        self.place_at_grid(speedo_label, "F4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(45), 
            Write(speedo_label),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        needle.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Final visualization: Needle oscillates slightly to show "live movement"
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(60),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(50),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Paradox of the Single Point",
            [
                "Acceleration creates a curved path on our position graph.",
                "Calculating slope at one point leads to zero over zero.",
                "This undefined result creates a challenging mathematical roadblock."
            ]
        )

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        color_line1 = BLUE_B
        color_line2 = RED_B
        color_line3 = RED

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A curved parabola represents increasing speed over time.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_line1)
        
        # Define a parabola curve using points on the grid to ensure it stays in the safe zone (Col 2-6)
        # Start at E2, go through D4, end at B6
        start_p = self.grid["E2"]
        mid_p = self.grid["D4"]
        end_p = self.grid["B6"]
        
        # Create a quadratic curve (parabola segment)
        parabola = CubicBezier(
            start_p, 
            start_p + RIGHT * 1.5, # Control point 1
            mid_p - RIGHT * 0.5,   # Control point 2
            end_p, 
            color=color_line1
        )
        
        # Add axes for context
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            tips=True,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "color": GREY_B}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Shift parabola to align with the visual area
        parabola.move_to(axes.get_center() + UP * 0.2 + RIGHT * 0.2)

        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(parabola), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A single point 'A' is highlighted on the curve.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_line2)
        
        # Pick a point on the parabola (approx D4 grid position)
        point_a_coord = parabola.point_from_proportion(0.5)
        dot_a = Dot(point_a_coord, color=color_line2, radius=0.1)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_line2, font_size=36)
        # Position label near the point (B001: avoid overlap)
        label_a.next_to(dot_a, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Formula 0/0
        formula_00 = MathTex("\\frac{0}{0}", color="#FF0000", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_00, "C5", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a), Write(label_a))
        self.play(Write(formula_00))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The formula '0 / 0' flashes in red (#FF0000) near the point.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_line3)
        
        # "Warning" Roadblock sign representation (simplified)
        warning_sign = VGroup(
            Triangle(color=color_line3).scale(0.8),
            Text("!", color=color_line3, weight=BOLD).scale(0.8)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(warning_sign, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Flash the 0/0 and show warning sign
        self.play(
            Indicate(formula_00, color=RED, scale_factor=1.5),
            FadeIn(warning_sign, shift=UP),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Repeated flash for emphasis
        self.play(Flash(formula_00, color=RED, num_lines=12, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.wait(2)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_str = "The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Swift the cheetah runs 100 meters in 4 seconds.",
            "His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.",
            "But how fast is he at one specific moment?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for elements
        GRAY_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: "Swift the cheetah runs 100 meters in 4 seconds."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY_COLOR)
        
        # Track path from B3 to B6
        start_coord = self.grid["B3"]
        end_coord = self.grid["B6"]
        track = Line(start_coord, end_coord, color=GRAY_COLOR)
        
        # Represent Swift the Cheetah with a Triangle
        swift = Triangle(color=WHITE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15).rotate(-PI/2)
        swift.move_to(start_coord)
        
        # Persistent label for Swift
        swift_label = Text("Swift", font_size=16, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        # B008: Use updater for position instead of recreating in always_redraw
        swift_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(swift, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        # Descriptive labels
        dist_label = Text("100 meters", font_size=20, color=GRAY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label, "C4")
        
        time_label = Text("4 seconds", font_size=20, color=GRAY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(time_label, "C5")
        
        self.play(Create(track), Write(dist_label), Write(time_label))
        self.add(swift, swift_label)
        
        # Swift runs the distance in 4 seconds
        self.play(
            swift.animate.move_to(end_coord),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: "His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        avg_speed_text = Text("Average Speed = 25m/s", font_size=22, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        # Positioned in the top row (A) to avoid overlap
        self.place_at_grid(avg_speed_text, "A4")
        
        self.play(Write(avg_speed_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "But how fast is he at one specific moment?"
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        # Freeze Swift at 2.5 seconds (0.625 of the total 4.0s path)
        freeze_ratio = 2.5 / 4.0
        freeze_point = start_coord + (end_coord - start_coord) * freeze_ratio

            "His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.",
            "But how fast is he at one specific moment?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for elements
        GRAY_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "The Visual Solution: The Shrinking Secant"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Draw a secant line through points A and B.",
            "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A.",
            "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink.",
            "As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line.",
            "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for consistency
        color_a = BLUE_B
        color_b = YELLOW_B
        color_secant = WHITE
        color_h = GREEN_B
        color_tangent = "#FFA500" # Bright Orange

        # 1. Coordinate System Setup (Restricted to Grid Cols 3-6)
        # Using Area B3 to E6 for the graph
        top_left = self.grid['B3']
        bottom_right = self.grid['E6']
        center = (top_left + bottom_right) / 2
        
        def to_grid_coords(x_rel, y_rel):
            """Converts relative coordinates to grid-space coordinates."""
            return center + np.array([x_rel, y_rel, 0])

        def func_rel(x):
            """Parabola defined relative to the center of the visual area."""
            return 0.4 * x**2 - 0.5
        
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: to_grid_coords(t, func_rel(t)),
            t_range=[-1.5, 1.5],
            color=GREY_C
        )
        
        # 2. Points and Dynamics
        x_a_rel = -0.8
        x_b_rel_start = 1.0
        x_b_tracker = ValueTracker(x_b_rel_start)
        
        pos_a = to_grid_coords(x_a_rel, func_rel(x_a_rel))
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color=color_a)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_a, font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Dot B and its label move with the tracker
        dot_b = Dot(color=color_b)
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(to_grid_coords(x_b_tracker.get_value(), func_rel(x_b_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=color_b, font_size=24)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1))

        # 3. Secant/Tangent Line Definition
        def get_current_line():
            xb = x_b_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = pos_a
            p2 = to_grid_coords(xb, func_rel(xb))
            direction = p2 - p1
            # If points are nearly coincident, use the derivative slope (0.8 * x_a_rel)
            if np.linalg.norm(direction) < 0.05:
                slope = 0.8 * x_a_rel
                direction = np.array([1, slope, 0])
            
            unit_dir = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            # Create a line spanning the visual area
            return Line(p1 - unit_dir * 1.5, p1 + unit_dir * 2.5, color=color_secant, stroke_width=2)

        secant_line = always_redraw(get_current_line)

        # 4. Horizontal gap 'h' visual
        h_y_level = bottom_right[1] + 0.2
        h_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            [pos_a[0], h_y_level, 0], 
            [to_grid_coords(x_b_tracker.get_value(), 0)[0], h_y_level, 0],
            color=color_h, stroke_width=4
        ))
        h_text = MathTex("h", color=color_h, font_size=24)
        h_text.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(h_line, UP, buff=0.05))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Draw a secant line through points A and B."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_secant)
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a, label_a), FadeIn(dot_b, label_b))
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_h)
        self.play(Create(h_line), FadeIn(h_text))
        
        # Slide B towards A
        self.play(
            x_b_tracker.animate.set_value(x_a_rel + 0.01),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(color_tangent)
        
        # Lock the line and transition color/style
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        final_tangent = get_current_line().set_color(color_tangent).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(secant_line, final_tangent),
            FadeOut(h_line, h_text),
            FadeOut(dot_b, label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(color_tangent)
        self.play(Indicate(secant_line, color=color_tangent, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash
section_1.content: Introduce the difference between average speed and instantaneous speed using a high-energy visual. Establish the core question: How do we measure speed at a single, frozen moment in time?
section_1.example: A cheetah (named 'Swift') chases a gazelle. We see a stopwatch. Swift covers 100 meters in 4 seconds (Average Speed = 25m/s). But at exactly 2.5 seconds, Swift hits a patch of sand and slows down slightly. How do we find his speed at that exact millisecond?

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
section_2.content: Briefly review the 'Rise over Run' concept. Explain that for a straight line, the rate of change (slope) is constant. Use a Position-Time graph to show a linear relationship.
section_2.example: A robot moving at a constant pace. The graph is a straight diagonal line. Slope = (Change in Position) / (Change in Time). This is the 'Average Rate of Change' which is easy to calculate because the line never bends.

section_3.title: The Paradox of the Single Point
section_3.content: Transition to a curved graph (parabola) representing acceleration. Show that calculating speed at one point (t) using the slope formula leads to 0/0 (undefined), creating a mathematical 'roadblock'.
section_3.example: Zoom into Swift the Cheetah's curved position graph. If we try to find the slope at point A by using only point A, our formula becomes (Position A - Position A) / (Time A - Time A) = 0/0. The screen flashes a warning sign.

section_4.title: The Visual Solution: The Shrinking Secant
section_4.content: Introduce the 'Limit' concept through animation. Place a second point (B) near point (A) and draw a secant line. Slowly slide point B toward point A, showing the secant line turning into a tangent line.
section_4.example: Imagine a camera lens zooming into the curve. As point B moves closer to A, the gap 'h' shrinks. The line connecting them tilts until it perfectly grazes the curve at just one point. This 'Tangent Line' represents the Instantaneous Rate of Change.

section_5.title: Formalizing the Derivative
section_5.content: Define the derivative formula. Explain that the derivative is simply the function that gives us the slope of the tangent line at any point x. Emphasize the notation f'(x).
section_5.example: Show the formula: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Use a color-coded overlay on the graph: Green for the change in height, Blue for the shrinking distance 'h'. As h disappears, the 'Derivative' is born.

section_6.title: Real-World Application: The Speedometer
section_6.content: Connect the abstract math back to reality. Explain that every time we look at a car's speedometer, we are looking at a live calculation of a derivative.
section_6.example: A dashboard of a sports car. As the car accelerates, the needle moves. The needle isn't showing average speed over the whole trip; it's showing the derivative of the car's position with respect to time at that exact heartbeat.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(Create(track), Write(dist_label), Write(time_label))
        self.add(swift, swift_label)
        
        # Swift runs the distance in 4 seconds
        self.play(
            swift.animate.move_to(end_coord),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)

        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "But how fast is he at one specific moment?"
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        # Freeze Swift at 2.5 seconds (0.625 of the total 4.0s path)
        freeze_ratio = 2.5 / 4.0
        freeze_point = start_coord + (end_coord - start_coord) * freeze_ratio

            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Large question mark to represent the core inquiry
        q_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=YELLOW_COLOR)
        # Positioned near the frozen cheetah's column at row A
        self.place_at_grid(q_mark, "A5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(q_mark, scale=1.2))
        self.wait(3)

            "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A.",
            "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink.",
            "As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line.",
            "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for consistency
        color_a = BLUE_B
        color_b = YELLOW_B
        color_secant = WHITE
        color_h = GREEN_B
        color_tangent = "#FFA500" # Bright Orange

        # 1. Coordinate System Setup (Restricted to Grid Cols 3-6)
        # Using Area B3 to E6 for the graph
        top_left = self.grid['B3']
        bottom_right = self.grid['E6']
        center = (top_left + bottom_right) / 2
        
        def to_grid_coords(x_rel, y_rel):
            """Converts relative coordinates to grid-space coordinates."""
            return center + np.array([x_rel, y_rel, 0])

        def func_rel(x):
            """Parabola defined relative to the center of the visual area."""
            return 0.4 * x**2 - 0.5
        
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: to_grid_coords(t, func_rel(t)),
            t_range=[-1.5, 1.5],
            color=GREY_C
        )
        
        # 2. Points and Dynamics
        x_a_rel = -0.8
        x_b_rel_start = 1.0
        x_b_tracker = ValueTracker(x_b_rel_start)
        
        pos_a = to_grid_coords(x_a_rel, func_rel(x_a_rel))
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color=color_a)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_a, font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Dot B and its label move with the tracker
        dot_b = Dot(color=color_b)
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(to_grid_coords(x_b_tracker.get_value(), func_rel(x_b_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=color_b, font_size=24)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1))

        # 3. Secant/Tangent Line Definition
        def get_current_line():
            xb = x_b_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = pos_a
            p2 = to_grid_coords(xb, func_rel(xb))
            direction = p2 - p1
            # If points are nearly coincident, use the derivative slope (0.8 * x_a_rel)
            if np.linalg.norm(direction) < 0.05:
                slope = 0.8 * x_a_rel
                direction = np.array([1, slope, 0])
            
            unit_dir = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            # Create a line spanning the visual area
            return Line(p1 - unit_dir * 1.5, p1 + unit_dir * 2.5, color=color_secant, stroke_width=2)

        secant_line = always_redraw(get_current_line)

        # 4. Horizontal gap 'h' visual
        h_y_level = bottom_right[1] + 0.2
        h_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            [pos_a[0], h_y_level, 0], 
            [to_grid_coords(x_b_tracker.get_value(), 0)[0], h_y_level, 0],
            color=color_h, stroke_width=4
        ))
        h_text = MathTex("h", color=color_h, font_size=24)
        h_text.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(h_line, UP, buff=0.05))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Draw a secant line through points A and B."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_secant)
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a, label_a), FadeIn(dot_b, label_b))
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_h)
        self.play(Create(h_line), FadeIn(h_text))
        
        # Slide B towards A
        self.play(
            x_b_tracker.animate.set_value(x_a_rel + 0.01),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(color_tangent)
        
        # Lock the line and transition color/style
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        final_tangent = get_current_line().set_color(color_tangent).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(secant_line, final_tangent),
            FadeOut(h_line, h_text),
            FadeOut(dot_b, label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(color_tangent)
        self.play(Indicate(secant_line, color=color_tangent, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title = "Formalizing the Derivative"
        lines = [
            "We define this instantaneous rate as the derivative, f prime.",
            "It measures the slope of the tangent at any point.",
            "The formula uses a limit as 'h' approaches zero.",
            "We find the slope over an infinitely small interval.",
            "This powerful tool describes how functions change instantly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Value Trackers
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(-0.5)

        # Colors
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#52C1FF"  # Distinguishable blue
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Math Objects - Formal Derivative Formula
        # Formula: f'(x) = lim_{h->0} [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h
        # Breakdown: f'(x) [0], = [1], lim [2], frac [3]
        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x)", "=", "\\lim_{h \\to 0}", "\\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            color=WHITE_COLOR, font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A3", "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Graph Setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20}
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        graph_area = VGroup(axes)
        # Visual Anchor: Start visuals at Column 3 to protect lecture text margins (B021)
        self.place_in_area(graph_area, "C3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        def func(x):
            return 0.5 * x**2 + 0.5

        curve = axes.plot(func, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Secant/Tangent Line and Points
        # Using a function and add_updater/always_redraw for simplicity in this specific geometry
        def get_secant_line():
            x0 = x_tracker.get_value()
            h = h_tracker.get_value()
            # Calculate slope
            m = (func(x0 + h) - func(x0)) / h
            # Line equation: y - f(x0) = m(x - x0)
            # Constrain x_range to avoid swinging into text area (B060)
            line = axes.plot(lambda x: m * (x - x0) + func(x0), color=YELLOW_COLOR, x_range=[max(-2, x0 - 1), min(2, x0 + h + 1)])
            return line

        secant_line = always_redraw(get_secant_line)
        
        point_p = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())), radius=0.06, color=WHITE))
        point_q = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value())), radius=0.06, color=WHITE))

        # Vertical and Horizontal segments for rise/run
        rise_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value())),
            color=GREEN_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        run_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=BLUE_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # We define this instantaneous rate as the derivative, f prime.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # It measures the slope of the tangent at any point.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(secant_line), Create(point_p), Create(point_q))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The formula uses a limit as 'h' approaches zero.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(run_line))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Highlight f(x+h) - f(x) in green
        self.play(Create(rise_line), formula[3].animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # We find the slope over an infinitely small interval.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR))
        # Animate h -> 0
        self.play(
            h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.01),
            formula[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This powerful tool describes how functions change instantly.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR))
        # The notation 'f prime of x' glows in yellow
        self.play(formula[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR), formula[0].animate.scale(1.2))
        self.play(formula[0].animate.scale(1/1.2))
        
        # The tangent line glides smoothly along the entire curve.
        # Ensure h stays small to represent tangent
        h_tracker.set_value(0.001) 
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash
outline.content: Introduce the difference between average speed and instantaneous speed using a high-energy visual. Establish the core question: How do we measure speed at a single, frozen moment in time?
outline.example: A cheetah (named 'Swift') chases a gazelle. We see a stopwatch. Swift covers 100 meters in 4 seconds (Average Speed = 25m/s). But at exactly 2.5 seconds, Swift hits a patch of sand and slows down slightly. How do we find his speed at that exact millisecond?

lecture_lines: Swift the cheetah runs 100 meters in 4 seconds.
His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.
But how fast is he at one specific moment?

Show 'Average Speed = 25m/s' in white (#FFFFFF) at the top.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_str = "The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Swift the cheetah runs 100 meters in 4 seconds.",
            "His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second.",
            "But how fast is he at one specific moment?"
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for elements
        GRAY_COLOR = "#D3D3D3"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line: "Swift the cheetah runs 100 meters in 4 seconds."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY_COLOR)
        
        # Track path from B3 to B6
        start_coord = self.grid["B3"]
        end_coord = self.grid["B6"]
        track = Line(start_coord, end_coord, color=GRAY_COLOR)
        
        # Represent Swift the Cheetah with a Triangle
        swift = Triangle(color=WHITE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15).rotate(-PI/2)
        swift.move_to(start_coord)
        
        # Persistent label for Swift
        swift_label = Text("Swift", font_size=16, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        # B008: Use updater for position instead of recreating in always_redraw
        swift_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(swift, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        # Descriptive labels
        dist_label = Text("100 meters", font_size=20, color=GRAY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_label, "C4")
        
        time_label = Text("4 seconds", font_size=20, color=GRAY_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(time_label, "C5")
        
        self.play(Create(track), Write(dist_label), Write(time_label))
        self.add(swift, swift_label)
        
        # Swift runs the distance in 4 seconds
        self.play(
            swift.animate.move_to(end_coord),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line: "His average speed is exactly 25 meters per second."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        avg_speed_text = Text("Average Speed = 25m/s", font_size=22, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        # Positioned in the top row (A) to avoid overlap
        self.place_at_grid(avg_speed_text, "A4")
        
        self.play(Write(avg_speed_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line: "But how fast is he at one specific moment?"
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW_COLOR)
        
        # Freeze Swift at 2.5 seconds (0.625 of the total 4.0s path)
        freeze_ratio = 2.5 / 4.0
        freeze_point = start_coord + (end_coord - start_coord) * freeze_ratio
        
        # Highlight and move Swift to the frozen moment
        self.play(
            swift.animate.move_to(freeze_point).set_color(YELLOW_COLOR),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Large question mark to represent the core inquiry
        q_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=YELLOW_COLOR)
        # Positioned near the frozen cheetah's column at row A
        self.place_at_grid(q_mark, "A5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(q_mark, scale=1.2))
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Real-World Application: The Speedometer
outline.content: Connect the abstract math back to reality. Explain that every time we look at a car's speedometer, we are looking at a live calculation of a derivative.
outline.example: A dashboard of a sports car. As the car accelerates, the needle moves. The needle isn't showing average speed over the whole trip; it's showing the derivative of the car's position with respect to time at that exact heartbeat.

                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Speedometer", [
            "- A car's speedometer shows speed at every heartbeat.",
            "- It continuously calculates the derivative of position.",
            "- Calculus connects abstract math to movement."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Build the Speedometer
        speedo_arc = Arc(
            radius=1.5, 
            start_angle=225 * DEGREES, 
            angle=-270 * DEGREES, 
            color=GRAY_A
        )
        
        # Create Ticks relative to a temporary origin, will move with VGroup
        ticks = VGroup()
        for i in range(11):
            angle = (225 - i * 27) * DEGREES
            start_pt = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * 1.35
            end_pt = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * 1.5
            ticks.add(Line(start_pt, end_pt, color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2))
        
        speedometer = VGroup(speedo_arc, ticks)
        # Use B3-E6 area for placement
        self.place_in_area(speedometer, "B3", "E6")
        center_point = speedometer.get_center()

outline.title: Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line
outline.content: Briefly review the 'Rise over Run' concept. Explain that for a straight line, the rate of change (slope) is constant. Use a Position-Time graph to show a linear relationship.
outline.example: A robot moving at a constant pace. The graph is a straight diagonal line. Slope = (Change in Position) / (Change in Time). This is the 'Average Rate of Change' which is easy to calculate because the line never bends.

lecture_lines: For a straight line, the slope is always constant.
We calculate it using the simple rise over run.
This value represents the constant average rate of change.
animations: A straight diagonal line appears on a Position-Time graph.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Check: The Slope of a Line"
        lines = [
            "For a straight line, the slope is always constant.",
            "We calculate it using the simple rise over run.",
            "This value represents the constant average rate of change."
        ]
        
        # Colors based on animation description
        COLOR_RISE = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_RUN = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_FORMULA = "#FFFF00"

        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: A straight diagonal line appears on a Position-Time graph.
        # We obey B021: Start visuals at Column 3 to protect lecture text margins.
        
        # Define Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY},
            x_axis_config={"label_direction": DOWN},
            y_axis_config={"label_direction": LEFT},
        )
        x_label = Text("Time (t)", font_size=16).next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN)
        y_label = Text("Pos (s)", font_size=16).next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT).rotate(90 * DEGREES)
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        
        # Place graph in area C3 to F6 (preserving B021 margin)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, "C3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Define the diagonal line: s = t
        func_line = axes.plot(lambda t: t, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_LINE)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE))
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(func_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: Vertical 'Rise' in green (#00FF00) and horizontal 'Run' in blue (#0000FF) appear.
        
        # Define points for rise/run: from (1,1) to (3,3)
        p1 = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        p2 = axes.c2p(3, 3)
        p_corner = axes.c2p(3, 1)

        self.play(Create(rise_line), Write(rise_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: The formula 'Slope = Rise / Run' appears in yellow (#FFFF00).
        
        # Place formula in top right area (A3 to B6)
        slope_formula = MathTex(
            r"\text{Slope} = \frac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}", 
            color=COLOR_FORMULA
        )
        self.place_in_area(slope_formula, "A3", "B6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_FORMULA))
        self.play(Write(slope_formula))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Paradox of the Single Point
outline.content: Transition to a curved graph (parabola) representing acceleration. Show that calculating speed at one point (t) using the slope formula leads to 0/0 (undefined), creating a mathematical 'roadblock'.
outline.example: Zoom into Swift the Cheetah's curved position graph. If we try to find the slope at point A by using only point A, our formula becomes (Position A - Position A) / (Time A - Time A) = 0/0. The screen flashes a warning sign.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Paradox of the Single Point",
            [
                "Acceleration creates a curved path on our position graph.",
                "Calculating slope at one point leads to zero over zero.",
                "This undefined result creates a challenging mathematical roadblock."
            ]
        )

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        color_line1 = BLUE_B
        color_line2 = RED_B
        color_line3 = RED

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A curved parabola represents increasing speed over time.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_line1)
        
        # Define a parabola curve using points on the grid to ensure it stays in the safe zone (Col 2-6)
        # Start at E2, go through D4, end at B6
        start_p = self.grid["E2"]
        mid_p = self.grid["D4"]
        end_p = self.grid["B6"]
        
        # Create a quadratic curve (parabola segment)
        parabola = CubicBezier(
            start_p, 
            start_p + RIGHT * 1.5, # Control point 1
            mid_p - RIGHT * 0.5,   # Control point 2
            end_p, 
            color=color_line1
        )
        
        # Add axes for context
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            tips=True,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "color": GREY_B}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Shift parabola to align with the visual area
        parabola.move_to(axes.get_center() + UP * 0.2 + RIGHT * 0.2)

        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(parabola), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A single point 'A' is highlighted on the curve.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_line2)
        
        # Pick a point on the parabola (approx D4 grid position)
        point_a_coord = parabola.point_from_proportion(0.5)
        dot_a = Dot(point_a_coord, color=color_line2, radius=0.1)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_line2, font_size=36)
        # Position label near the point (B001: avoid overlap)
        label_a.next_to(dot_a, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Formula 0/0
        formula_00 = MathTex("\\frac{0}{0}", color="#FF0000", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_00, "C5", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a), Write(label_a))
        self.play(Write(formula_00))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The formula '0 / 0' flashes in red (#FF0000) near the point.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_line3)
        
        # "Warning" Roadblock sign representation (simplified)
        warning_sign = VGroup(
            Triangle(color=color_line3).scale(0.8),
            Text("!", color=color_line3, weight=BOLD).scale(0.8)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(warning_sign, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Flash the 0/0 and show warning sign
        self.play(
            Indicate(formula_00, color=RED, scale_factor=1.5),
            FadeIn(warning_sign, shift=UP),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Repeated flash for emphasis
        self.play(Flash(formula_00, color=RED, num_lines=12, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Visual Solution: The Shrinking Secant
outline.content: Introduce the 'Limit' concept through animation. Place a second point (B) near point (A) and draw a secant line. Slowly slide point B toward point A, showing the secant line turning into a tangent line.
outline.example: Imagine a camera lens zooming into the curve. As point B moves closer to A, the gap 'h' shrinks. The line connecting them tilts until it perfectly grazes the curve at just one point. This 'Tangent Line' represents the Instantaneous Rate of Change.

storyboard.title: The Visual Solution: The Shrinking Secant
lecture_lines: Draw a secant line through points A and B.
Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A.
The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink.
As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line.
This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment.
animations: A curved graph shows two points, A and B, with a secant line.
Label the horizontal gap between A and B as 'h'.
Animate point B sliding toward A, causing 'h' to shrink.
The secant line rotates to graze the curve at point A.
The line turns into a bright orange (#FFA500) tangent line.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Title and Lecture Lines
        title_text = "The Visual Solution: The Shrinking Secant"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Draw a secant line through points A and B.",
            "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A.",
            "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink.",
            "As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line.",
            "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors for consistency
        color_a = BLUE_B
        color_b = YELLOW_B
        color_secant = WHITE
        color_h = GREEN_B
        color_tangent = "#FFA500" # Bright Orange

        # 1. Coordinate System Setup (Restricted to Grid Cols 3-6)
        # Using Area B3 to E6 for the graph
        top_left = self.grid['B3']
        bottom_right = self.grid['E6']
        center = (top_left + bottom_right) / 2
        
        def to_grid_coords(x_rel, y_rel):
            """Converts relative coordinates to grid-space coordinates."""
            return center + np.array([x_rel, y_rel, 0])

        def func_rel(x):
            """Parabola defined relative to the center of the visual area."""
            return 0.4 * x**2 - 0.5
        
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: to_grid_coords(t, func_rel(t)),
            t_range=[-1.5, 1.5],
            color=GREY_C
        )
        
        # 2. Points and Dynamics
        x_a_rel = -0.8
        x_b_rel_start = 1.0
        x_b_tracker = ValueTracker(x_b_rel_start)
        
        pos_a = to_grid_coords(x_a_rel, func_rel(x_a_rel))
        dot_a = Dot(pos_a, color=color_a)
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_a, font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Dot B and its label move with the tracker
        dot_b = Dot(color=color_b)
        dot_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(to_grid_coords(x_b_tracker.get_value(), func_rel(x_b_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=color_b, font_size=24)
        label_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(dot_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1))

        # 3. Secant/Tangent Line Definition
        def get_current_line():
            xb = x_b_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = pos_a
            p2 = to_grid_coords(xb, func_rel(xb))
            direction = p2 - p1
            # If points are nearly coincident, use the derivative slope (0.8 * x_a_rel)
            if np.linalg.norm(direction) < 0.05:
                slope = 0.8 * x_a_rel
                direction = np.array([1, slope, 0])
            
            unit_dir = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            # Create a line spanning the visual area
            return Line(p1 - unit_dir * 1.5, p1 + unit_dir * 2.5, color=color_secant, stroke_width=2)

        secant_line = always_redraw(get_current_line)

        # 4. Horizontal gap 'h' visual
        h_y_level = bottom_right[1] + 0.2
        h_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            [pos_a[0], h_y_level, 0], 
            [to_grid_coords(x_b_tracker.get_value(), 0)[0], h_y_level, 0],
            color=color_h, stroke_width=4
        ))
        h_text = MathTex("h", color=color_h, font_size=24)
        h_text.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(h_line, UP, buff=0.05))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Draw a secant line through points A and B."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_secant)
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a, label_a), FadeIn(dot_b, label_b))
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_h)
        self.play(Create(h_line), FadeIn(h_text))
        
        # Slide B towards A
        self.play(
            x_b_tracker.animate.set_value(x_a_rel + 0.01),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "As 'h' nears zero, the secant becomes a tangent line."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(color_tangent)
        
        # Lock the line and transition color/style
        secant_line.clear_updaters()
        final_tangent = get_current_line().set_color(color_tangent).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(secant_line, final_tangent),
            FadeOut(h_line, h_text),
            FadeOut(dot_b, label_b)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(color_tangent)
        self.play(Indicate(secant_line, color=color_tangent, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(2)

outline.content: Define the derivative formula. Explain that the derivative is simply the function that gives us the slope of the tangent line at any point x. Emphasize the notation f'(x).
outline.example: Show the formula: f'(x) = lim (h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Use a color-coded overlay on the graph: Green for the change in height, Blue for the shrinking distance 'h'. As h disappears, the 'Derivative' is born.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title = "Formalizing the Derivative"
        lines = [
            "We define this instantaneous rate as the derivative, f prime.",
            "It measures the slope of the tangent at any point.",
            "The formula uses a limit as 'h' approaches zero.",
            "We find the slope over an infinitely small interval.",
            "This powerful tool describes how functions change instantly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Value Trackers
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.5)
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(-0.5)

        # Colors
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#52C1FF"  # Distinguishable blue
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # Math Objects - Formal Derivative Formula
        # Formula: f'(x) = lim_{h->0} [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h
        # Breakdown: f'(x) [0], = [1], lim [2], frac [3]
        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x)", "=", "\\lim_{h \\to 0}", "\\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            color=WHITE_COLOR, font_size=36
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A3", "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Graph Setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20}
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        graph_area = VGroup(axes)
        # Visual Anchor: Start visuals at Column 3 to protect lecture text margins (B021)
        self.place_in_area(graph_area, "C3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        def func(x):
            return 0.5 * x**2 + 0.5

        curve = axes.plot(func, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Secant/Tangent Line and Points
        # Using a function and add_updater/always_redraw for simplicity in this specific geometry
        def get_secant_line():
            x0 = x_tracker.get_value()
            h = h_tracker.get_value()
            # Calculate slope
            m = (func(x0 + h) - func(x0)) / h
            # Line equation: y - f(x0) = m(x - x0)
            # Constrain x_range to avoid swinging into text area (B060)
            line = axes.plot(lambda x: m * (x - x0) + func(x0), color=YELLOW_COLOR, x_range=[max(-2, x0 - 1), min(2, x0 + h + 1)])
            return line

        secant_line = always_redraw(get_secant_line)
        
        point_p = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())), radius=0.06, color=WHITE))
        point_q = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value())), radius=0.06, color=WHITE))

        # Vertical and Horizontal segments for rise/run
        rise_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value())),
            color=GREEN_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        run_line = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value() + h_tracker.get_value(), func(x_tracker.get_value())),
            color=BLUE_COLOR, stroke_width=4
        ))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # We define this instantaneous rate as the derivative, f prime.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # It measures the slope of the tangent at any point.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(secant_line), Create(point_p), Create(point_q))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The formula uses a limit as 'h' approaches zero.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(run_line))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Highlight f(x+h) - f(x) in green
        self.play(Create(rise_line), formula[3].animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # We find the slope over an infinitely small interval.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR))
        # Animate h -> 0
        self.play(
            h_tracker.animate.set_value(0.01),
            formula[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This powerful tool describes how functions change instantly.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR))
        # The notation 'f prime of x' glows in yellow
        self.play(formula[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR), formula[0].animate.scale(1.2))
        self.play(formula[0].animate.scale(1/1.2))
        
        # The tangent line glides smoothly along the entire curve.
        # Ensure h stays small to represent tangent
        h_tracker.set_value(0.001) 
        self.play(

            tick_b = Line([x_b_grid, y_base - 0.1, 0], [x_b_grid, y_base + 0.1, 0], color=color_h)
            h_text = MathTex("h", color=color_h, font_size=24).next_to(line, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            return VGroup(line, tick_a, tick_b, h_text)

        h_label_group = always_redraw(get_h_line_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Draw a secant line through points A and B."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_secant)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a, label_a), FadeIn(dot_b, label_b))
        self.play(Create(secant_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Next, we slowly slide point B closer to point A."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The gap between them, called 'h', begins to shrink."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_h)
        self.play(FadeIn(h_label_group))
        
        # Slide B towards A
        self.play(
            x_b_tracker.animate.set_value(x_a + 0.05),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        current_secant = secant_line.copy()

        x_b_tracker.set_value(x_a)

        # Derivative of 0.2x^2 + 0.5 is 0.4x. At x=1, slope=0.4.

        p_close = axes.c2p(x_a + 0.01, func(x_a + 0.01))
        tan_dir = p_close - p1
        tan_unit = tan_dir / np.linalg.norm(tan_dir)
        tangent_line = Line(p1 - tan_unit * 2.0, p1 + tan_unit * 3.5, color=color_tangent, stroke_width=4)

            Transform(current_secant, tangent_line),
            FadeOut(h_label_group),
            FadeOut(dot_b, label_b),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This tangent represents the speed at that exact moment."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(color_tangent)
        self.play(Indicate(current_secant, color=color_tangent, scale_factor=1.05))

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Paradox of the Single Point",
            [
                "Acceleration creates a curved path on our position graph.",
                "Calculating slope at one point leads to zero over zero.",
                "This undefined result creates a challenging mathematical roadblock."
            ]
        )

        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        color_line1 = BLUE_B
        color_line2 = RED_B
        color_line3 = RED

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A curved parabola [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg] represents increasing speed over time.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_line1)

            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            tips=True,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "color": GREY_B}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Load and place graph asset - Issue 26/46
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg
        parabola_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg")

        label_a = MathTex("A", color=color_line2, font_size=30)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Speedometer", [
            "- A car's speedometer shows speed at every heartbeat.",
            "- It continuously calculates the derivative of position.",
            "- Calculus connects abstract math to movement."
        ])

        # Assets
        speed_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speed.svg"
        car_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Speedometer SVG
        speedometer = SVGMobject(speed_path).set_color(WHITE)
        # Fix layout: Place the speedometer in area B3-F6 with scale 0.8 (Issues #40, #41)
        self.place_in_area(speedometer, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Create a Needle
        pivot = speedometer.get_center()
        # Initial needle position (pointing to 0, approx 135 deg in standard polar)
        needle = Line(pivot, pivot + rotate_vector(UP * 0.7, 135 * DEGREES), color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer), Create(needle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Car image (Issue #27, #47)
        car = ImageMobject(car_path)
        self.place_at_grid(car, "F3", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Synchronization Tracker
        progress = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updaters for synchronized motion
        # Needle sweep from 135 deg to -135 deg (270 deg total)
        def update_needle(m):
            angle = (135 - progress.get_value() * 270) * DEGREES
            m.put_start_and_end_on(pivot, pivot + rotate_vector(UP * 0.7, angle))
            
        needle.add_updater(update_needle)
        
        # Car moves horizontally across the bottom
        start_car_x = self.grid["F3"][0]
        end_car_x = self.grid["F6"][0]
        car.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_x(start_car_x + progress.get_value() * (end_car_x - start_car_x)))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        self.play(progress.animate.set_value(1), run_time=4, rate_func=slow_into)
        self.wait(1)
        
        needle.clear_updaters()
        car.clear_updaters()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Derivative label
        derivative_text = Text("Instantaneous Speed = Derivative", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        # Position label in Row A to avoid occlusion (Belief B005 consideration vs Issue 41)
        self.place_in_area(derivative_text, "A3", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(derivative_text))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x)",                      # 0
            "=",                         # 1
            "\\lim_{h \\to 0}",           # 2
            "{f(x+h) - f(x)",             # 3
